sources.entry: 📖 Professional software development: pretty complete and a good companion to this page. The free chapters are mostly focused on software development processes: design, testing, code writing, etc. - and not so much about tech itself.

summary.title: Professional Software Development
summary.one_liner: A free, in-progress book covering the software development process (design, testing, code writing, continuous integration) more than specific technologies.
takeaways: The book aims to cover almost everything needed to start working as a professional software developer.
Its free chapters focus mainly on development processes such as design, testing and code writing rather than specific tech.
Continuous integration is presented as backed by several principles and practices, not just a tool.
The book is a work in progress, and this page shows only the acknowledgements and a partial chapter.
summary.summary: This page is the front matter and acknowledgements of a free, still-in-progress book titled Professional Software Development, which says it covers almost everything needed to hit the ground running. The visible text lists cover art credits and the tools used to build the book, including Python, Sphinx, Graphviz, Dia and Inkscape. A short excerpt from a chapter on the software development lifecycle introduces continuous integration as a set of principles and practices. The page text contains little beyond this, so the specific topics in later chapters are not visible here.
